thread.title: What's Next For Broadcom Now That Trump's Nixed Qualcomm Buy?

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: What's Next For Broadcom Now That Trump's Nixed Qualcomm Buy?
text:
Chipmaker Broadcom ( AVGO ) is likely to pursue other acquisitions now that President Donald Trump has nixed its proposed purchase of Qualcomm ( QCOM ), analysts say.
X Trump late Monday issued an order blocking Broadcom's hostile takeover bid for San Diego-based Qualcomm on national security grounds. Even though Singapore-based Broadcom is moving its headquarters to the U.S., the federal government is still concerned about the company's ties to China, including firms like Huawei.
Another worry is that the U.S. would lose its leadership position in 5G wireless technology if Qualcomm is acquired. The Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States had cited concerns about Broadcom's penchant for slashing research and development spending following acquisitions.
It isn't the first time that Trump has blocked a chip industry deal on national security grounds related to China. Last September, he blocked the sale of Hillsboro, Ore.-based Lattice Semiconductor ( LSCC ) to Canyon Bridge Capital Partners, which has ties to a fund owned by the Chinese government.
Broadcom is likely to remain acquisitive, but will pursue smaller chip firms, Wall Street analysts said Tuesday. Its offer for Qualcomm was valued at $117 billion.
Several analysts on Tuesday cited Xilinx ( XLNX ) as the next possible acquisition target for Broadcom.
"Xilinx satisfies most of Broadcom's requirements and is in a stable duopoly, though valuation could be high given Broadcom's historical discipline," RBC Capital Markets analyst Amit Daryanani said in a report. Xilinx has a market value of nearly $20 billion.
Broadcom's acquisition prospects likely start with Xilinx, "which appears well-aligned," B. Riley FBR analyst Craig Ellis said in a report.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Another possibility is Mellanox Technologies ( MLNX ), Ellis and other analysts said Tuesday.
If Broadcom decides to step back from acquisitions, it could please investors by increasing its capital returns through dividends and share buybacks, Ellis said.
With the takeover threat gone, Qualcomm now has to focus on getting its house in order, BMO Capital Markets analyst Tim Long said in a report.
It faces headwinds in its core wireless chip business and a major legal conflict with customer Apple ( AAPL ), Long said. Plus, Qualcomm still hasn't closed its purchase of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ), which needs to get approval from regulators in China.
Qualcomm stock "could tread water in the $60 range" until the company can show that it is on the right track, GBH Insights analyst Daniel Ives said in a report.
Qualcomm shares fell 5% to close at 59.70 on the stock market today . Broadcom stock dipped 0.6% to 261.22.
Meanwhile, possible Broadcom acquisition target Xilinx lost 1.2% to 76.14. Mellanox dropped 1.4% to 71.95.
A wild card in the chip consolidation trend is Intel ( INTC ). Last week, the Wall Street Journal reported that Intel is interested in making acquisitions to shore up its competition positioning. The Journal said Intel could even make a play for Broadcom.
However, an Intel-Broadcom combination appears unlikely, especially after Trump's executive order, Ellis said.
"The president's action not only banned the (Broadcom-Qualcomm) deal, but restricted 'any substantially equivalent merger, acquisition, or takeover,'" Ellis said. "That writing could potentially preclude an Intel and Broadcom combination. Even before that, we believe deal size (Intel $244 billion market cap and Broadcom $104 billion), international regulatory approval, and customer supplier concentration fears and thus pushback are sufficient to keep us skeptical."
